html: The Coca were an Indigenous people of central Jalisco in western Mexico, living around Lake Chapala and the Santiago River valley near present Guadalajara. Their language, now extinct, is known only from scraps and is usually thought to have been Uto-Aztecan. They lived beside the Tecuexe and Caxcanes, and came under Spanish rule after Nuño de Guzmán's brutal campaign in western Mexico around 1530, followed by the Mixtón War of 1540 to 1542. By the 1600s they had merged into the mixed population of New Spain. They have nothing to do with the coca plant.
